Habermas distinguishes between law as medium and law as institution, with language serving as the medium of reaching understanding. He describes the ideal speech situation as one in which participants are free from coercion and domination, grounding his theory of communicative rationality. Note that the team's gloss—law as medium meaning media portrayal and law as institution meaning the courts—does not match Habermas's usage, where "medium" refers to law as a steering mechanism of power and money and "institution" to law as anchored in communicative action.
